chapterTitle: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 4 (FBISE Class 12 Chemistry)
title: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 4 (FBISE Class 12 Chemistry)
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: Which period of the periodic table is the shortest, containing only 2 elements?
questions.explanation: Period 1 contains only Hydrogen (1s¹) and Helium (1s²).

questions.question: What gas is evolved at the cathode during the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride (brine)?
questions.explanation: H⁺ (from water) has a higher reduction potential than Na⁺, so 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ occurs at the cathode.

questions.question: An aqueous solution of borax is alkaline to litmus because of:

options.A: Complete ionization into strong base NaOH and weak acid H₃BO₃ upon hydrolysis

questions.explanation: Na₂B₄O₇ + 7H₂O ⇌ 2NaOH (strong base) + 4H₃BO₃ (weak acid); high [OH⁻] renders the solution distinctly alkaline (pH ~9).

questions.question: When concentrated nitric acid reacts with metallic copper, the dense brown gas evolved is:
questions.explanation: Cu + 4 HNO₃ (conc.) → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2 NO₂ (red-brown gas) + 2 H₂O. Dilute HNO₃ gives colorless NO.

questions.question: Tincture of iodine, a classic antiseptic solution, contains:

options.B: 2-3% solution of Iodine and Potassium Iodide (KI) in an alcohol-water mixture

questions.explanation: Tincture of iodine is 2-3% I₂ with KI dissolved in ethanol-water; KI enhances iodine solubility via formation of soluble triiodide ions (I₃⁻).

questions.question: In the spectrochemical series, which of the following ligands produces the largest crystal field splitting (Δ_o)?
questions.explanation: CO and CN⁻ are the strongest field ligands due to synergistic π-back-bonding, causing maximum d-orbital splitting.

questions.question: An electrophile is defined as a chemical species that is:

options.A: Electron-rich and donates an electron pair (Lewis base)
options.B: Electron-deficient and accepts an electron pair to form a new bond (Lewis acid)

questions.explanation: Electrophiles ('electron-lovers') seek electron density; they may be cations (H⁺, NO₂⁺, Br⁺) or neutral Lewis acids (BF₃, AlCl₃, SO₃).

questions.question: Which of the following gases is known as 'marsh gas' because it is produced by anaerobic bacterial decomposition of plant matter in swamps and paddy fields?
questions.explanation: Methane is marsh gas, generated by methanogenic archaebacteria in oxygen-depleted marshy soils.

questions.question: According to molecular orbital theory, the aromatic sextet of benzene is formed by:

options.A: Three completely filled bonding molecular orbitals (ψ₁, ψ₂, ψ₃) of lower energy containing 6 delocalized π-electrons

questions.explanation: Six 2p_z atomic orbitals combine to generate 3 bonding (ψ₁, ψ₂, ψ₃) and 3 antibonding (ψ₄*, ψ₅*, ψ₆*) MOs; all 6 π-electrons reside in the low-energy bonding MOs.

questions.question: In the E1 mechanism (Elimination Unimolecular), the rate-determining step is:

options.A: Removal of a β-proton by base
options.B: Loss of leaving group to form a carbocation intermediate

questions.explanation: E1 shares its slow rate-determining step with S_N1: heterolytic departure of the leaving group to form a carbocation.

questions.question: Dow's process for the industrial preparation of phenol involves heating chlorobenzene with 6-8% aqueous NaOH at 350°C and 300 atm pressure. The intermediate formed before acidification is:
questions.explanation: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution under forced conditions yields sodium phenoxide, which upon acidification with HCl yields free phenol.

questions.question: Benedict's solution, used in clinical pathology to detect reducing sugars (glucose) in diabetic urine, contains:

options.A: CuSO₄, sodium citrate, and sodium carbonate in alkaline aqueous solution

questions.explanation: Benedict's reagent stabilizes Cu²⁺ with citrate ions in Na₂CO₃ solution, forming a red Cu₂O precipitate upon boiling with reducing sugars (aldehydes).

questions.question: Which of the following functional derivatives of carboxylic acids has the highest boiling point due to extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding involving two donor sites?
questions.explanation: Primary amides (-CONH₂) possess highly polar carbonyl and amino groups that form strong multi-directional hydrogen-bonded networks, resulting in unusually high melting and boiling points.

questions.question: Which of the following carbohydrates gives a blue-black coloration with iodine solution?
questions.explanation: Iodine (I₃⁻ / I₅⁻) slips inside the helical coils of unbranched amylose in starch, forming a deep blue-black charge-transfer complex.

questions.question: Which of the following gases is used as a feedstock for synthesizing ammonia in Pakistani fertilizer plants, sourced abundantly from Sui gas fields?

options.A: Natural gas (Methane, CH₄ via steam-methane reforming)

questions.explanation: Steam reforming of natural gas: CH₄ + H₂O ⇌ CO + 3 H₂ provides hydrogen for ammonia synthesis.

questions.question: What is the primary toxic effect of lead (Pb²⁺) poisoning on human health, especially in young children?

options.A: Inhibits enzymes for heme synthesis (causing anemia) and damages developing central nervous system, lowering IQ

questions.explanation: Lead inhibits aminolevulinic acid dehydratase, causing anemia, encephalopathy, and permanent neurodevelopmental cognitive deficits.

questions.question: Why are vinyl halides (CH₂=CH-Cl) and aryl halides (C₆H₅Cl) exceptionally resistant to nucleophilic substitution under standard conditions?

options.A: The lone pair on halogen delocalizes into the π-system, imparting partial double-bond character to the C-X bond and sp² carbon has higher electronegativity
options.D: Halogen is bonded to an sp³ carbon

questions.explanation: Resonance delocalizes the chlorine lone pair, giving the C-Cl bond double bond character and making heterolytic cleavage difficult.
